Pocketdesk is a remote desktop for your own computers: an Android app that streams and controls a Linux or Windows desktop, with files both ways, the clipboard, notifications and sound, one keyboard and mouse across your computers, each of your computers showing and controlling the others in a window, and now your phone's apps, camera and place available on your computer, and one computer's window lent to another.

**This is a beta.** Most features are verified on two Android phones against a Windows host, and many on-device checks are still open. Much of what is new in this release has run in tests and between throwaway servers, some of it on an OPPO phone, and the features that use Shizuku (apps in windows of their own, keys to taps, the phone's hotspot), the wake helper and the watch tile have not yet run on a real phone or watch at all (see the end of these notes). See [`docs/device-verification-checklist.md`](https://github.com/sreevarshan-xenoz/Pocketdesk/blob/main/docs/device-verification-checklist.md). Please read [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/sreevarshan-xenoz/Pocketdesk/blob/main/SECURITY.md) before using it on a network you do not control.

## Install

| Platform | File | How |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | `pocketdesk-…-windows-x86_64-setup.exe` | Run it: it installs Pocketdesk, starts it at sign-in with its firewall ports open, puts `pocketdesk` on `PATH` and offers FFmpeg through winget. Uninstall it from Settings → Apps. |
| Windows, portable | `pocketdesk-…-windows-x86_64.zip` | Unzip, then run `pocketdesk.exe install` to start the server at logon and open its firewall ports. `pocketdesk-app.exe` is the desktop app. FFmpeg must be on `PATH` for the encoder. |
| Debian, Ubuntu | `pocketdesk-…-linux-amd64.deb` | `sudo apt install ./pocketdesk-…-linux-amd64.deb` installs the server, the desktop app and the tray, with the libraries they need, and starts the server at every sign-in. `sudo apt remove pocketdesk` takes it out. |
| Linux | `pocketdesk-…-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sreevarshan-xenoz/Pocketdesk/main/scripts/install.sh \| bash` installs the server, the desktop app, the tray and the systemd user service. It needs PipeWire and FFmpeg (libav*). On Arch, `yay -S pocketdesk` installs it from the AUR. |
| Android | `pocketdesk-…-android-arm64*.apk` | Install it on the phone, then pair with the QR code from the desktop app's Pair page. |

`SHA256SUMS` lists every file's checksum (`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`).

An APK named `…-debug-signed.apk` is the debug build. It works, but Android will not update it in place from a differently signed build, so uninstall it first when switching to a store or release-signed build.

## What's changed

Pocketdesk 0.9.0 puts your phone's apps on your computer: open one from a Phone apps page, pin it to the Start menu, drop a file into it, and with Shizuku, give each app a window of its own and play phone games from the keyboard and mouse. Your computer can use the phone's camera as a webcam and its place as a location (Linux), keep folders from the phone, wake a sleeping computer through a spare phone at home, and approve `sudo` with your fingerprint. When no Wi-Fi is shared, the computer can make its own for the phone. Between your own computers, a window can now move from one to another and be used there, with less delay than before. It updates 0.8.3 in place (same signing key), keeping your saved computers and pairings. The optional features that use Shizuku are off by default and need Shizuku installed and running on the phone; nothing in this release needs wireless debugging or root.

**Your phone's apps on your computer**
- **A Phone apps page** (Windows and Linux): the phone's apps as icons with a search box, the ones you opened from here first. A click opens the app on the phone and shows the phone's screen in a window. It needs "Let the computer open my apps" on the phone (off by default) and adds no Android permission. If the phone's screen is not yet shown to that computer, the phone shows one notification and your tap on it brings Android's own screen-sharing question once; later apps reuse it. The page says plainly when the phone is locked, the control service is off, or the phone needs a tap (limit 78).
- **Hands-free:** with "Accept screen sharing for my computers" on the phone (off by default) and Pocketdesk control turned on, the phone answers that question for your own computer's open and swipes away a lock with nothing behind it. A paused share keeps the consent for up to ten minutes (its notification stays up with Stop) so the next open needs no new question. A PIN, pattern, password or fingerprint lock is never bypassed: the page says to unlock the phone or let Android keep it unlocked near the computer (Extend Unlock or Smart Lock) (limit 79).
- **Pin, notifications and drops:** right-click an app to pin it to the Start menu (Windows) or the applications menu (Linux) as "<App> (phone)"; the Notifications page's "Open app on the phone"; and a file dropped on the phone's screen window is sent and shared into the app in front. Windows has no way to pin to the taskbar for you, so use Start's own Pin to taskbar (limit 81).
- **Each app in a window of its own (optional, needs Shizuku, off by default):** the phone's Settings → "Separate windows (Shizuku)", on Android 10 or later and shown only while Shizuku is installed and running. Turning it on asks Shizuku's own permission dialog once. Up to four apps at once, each in its own window on the computer, with touch, scroll, Back and typing reaching only that window's app; "Open phone apps in windows of their own" on the computer's side is on by default. Without it, apps open on the phone's screen as before (limit 83).
- **Keys to taps (optional, needs the window mode above, off by default):** the desktop's Settings → Phones → "Keymaps for phone apps". In an app's window, map keys to taps, a stick (WASD), swipes, and an aim that follows the locked mouse, with up to nine fingers at once, to play a phone game from the keyboard. Some online games flag injected input (limit 83).
- **The phone's hotspot from the computer (optional, needs Shizuku, off by default):** the phone's Settings → "Let my computers turn on my hotspot" (Android 11 or later) lets your own computer's Overview turn the phone's Wi-Fi hotspot on and off with no tap ("Use my phone's hotspot", "Turn its hotspot off"). It goes off by itself after the time you pick (15, 30, 60, 120 minutes or never, 30 by default) and always after four hours. On Linux with NetworkManager, "Join my phone's hotspot network" in Settings joins a saved network by name, with no password read or kept (limit 85).

**More from your phone, for your computer**
- **The phone's camera as a webcam on Linux:** the computer's "Use as a camera" asks the phone (Settings → Phones: "Offer phones as a camera", off by default; on the phone, "Let the computer use my camera" and a Webcam permission, both off), and only a tap on the phone's notification starts it. Apps see "Pocketdesk camera" as an ordinary camera, with no kernel module. "Stop camera" ends it and the phone says when it is in use (limit 74).
- **The phone's place for the computer's apps (Linux):** desktop Settings → Phones → "Location from my phone" (off) and the phone's "Give my computer my location" (off, with "Exact location" under it) give GeoClue a city or an exact fix. For the phone to answer with its screen off, you allow Android's "Allow all the time" yourself (limit 76).
- **Phone folders kept on the computer:** the phone's Settings → "Folders kept on my computer": pick folders with Android's folder picker (no all-files permission), choose a schedule (on Wi-Fi while charging by default, or every 1 to 24 hours), and they are copied one way to the computer. "Mirror deletions" is off, and the computer has its own switch and a size cap. Owner phones only (limit 80).
- **A spare phone as the wake helper:** an old phone left on a charger at home turns on "Wake helper for this home" (off by default) and your other phones, when away, can wake your computer through it with "Wake through my helper" (off by default, per computer). The desktop's Settings → Wake shows the helper with Remove (limit 82).
- **Approve with my phone (Linux):** with a line you add to `/etc/pam.d` yourself, a Yes on the phone, with your fingerprint or screen lock for each use, approves `sudo`, and with their own switches polkit and the lock screen. Off on both sides by default; Pocketdesk never edits PAM; the guide has the lock-out warning and the way back (limit 73).
- **A Wear OS tile:** Wake, Ring phone, the computer's music, Deck buttons and a question's No, over Bluetooth to your phone (phone Settings → "Watch controls", off, each button with its own switch), with no Google Play services. The watch cannot approve anything: a Yes needs the phone's fingerprint. The watch app is built from the source tree and is not one of the release files (limit 84).

**Your windows, across your computers**
- **Borrow a window of another of your computers:** "Borrow a window…" on a computer's screen window lists the other computer's windows, and the one you pick opens in a window of its own here, sized to that window, while it leaves the other screen (Sway and Hyprland 0.56). A Windows computer lends a window where it is, with your clicks and typing reaching it there; a GNOME computer lends one to look at only, and only with "Unattended on GNOME" on. Lending is **on by default**, only to your own computers paired both ways with the Input permission (no phone, guest or stranger), and turned off with Settings → Other computers → "Let my computers borrow my windows" (limits 86, 88, 89).
- **Drag a window past the edge:** with one keyboard and mouse across your computers, drag a window off a Sway or Hyprland screen and let go on the other computer, and it opens there; drag it back to return it. **On by default**; it does nothing until the shared keyboard and mouse are on and the computer lends, and Settings → Other computers → "Drag windows to my other computers" turns it off (limit 87).
- **Less delay in a computer's window:** on the Linux laptop the click-to-picture time went from about 39 ms to 22 to 24 ms at the median. VA-API no longer holds a frame and converts colours on the graphics card, a still screen sends nothing, the window draws as each picture comes (a setting can stop it waiting for the display), the other computer's pointer is drawn here so it moves at once, and a window the compositor hides no longer stalls the app.
- **Zero-copy capture:** on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME and KDE the screen goes from the compositor to the hardware encoder without a copy through memory. On the laptop that took a 1080p Sway stream from 31 to 60 frames a second and its CPU from 18 % to 7 %, and halved the server's CPU per frame on GNOME. Where a driver or compositor will not, it copies as before.
- **Smooth keyframes, on by default:** x264 and NVENC spread a keyframe over several frames instead of sending a whole one every two seconds, and VA-API sends one when asked and every ten seconds, so the picture no longer stutters on a two-second beat. Settings → Phones → "Smooth keyframes" turns it off.

**Reaching each other**
- **A direct link:** when no network is shared, the Pair page's "Make a direct link" makes this computer's own Wi-Fi for one phone, on Linux through NetworkManager and on Windows through Mobile Hotspot. The pairing code carries the network's name and passphrase, and the phone joins it for Pocketdesk only, leaving other apps and mobile data as they were. If the computer must give up its own Wi-Fi to do it, the Pair page says so and asks first. It ends after ten idle minutes (a setting) and at eight hours at most, and on Windows it puts your own hotspot settings back (limit 77).

**Streaming and input**
- **Fine scrolling:** a touchpad's slow scroll now scrolls a little at a time, from a window, from the phone's trackpad and with shared input, on Linux, Windows and X11. "Smooth scrolling" (on) in the desktop's Settings → Other computers and the phone's Settings → Input turns it off.
- **Shared input is lighter:** the receiving end no longer waits on file reads before injecting, and the sending end paces its moves, groups its work and wakes less often at rest (about 7 a second at home, down from about 20).
- **Each screen window's clicks land on its own screen** of a Linux computer (Sway, Hyprland), where they used to land over the whole desktop.
- **Fit the screen to this window**, on a Linux computer: the window asks the other computer for a screen the size of its picture area (off by default, in the window's bar and Settings → Other computers); Windows computers say they cannot.
- **Software encoding on stock Fedora** now works through OpenH264, so a machine with no hardware encoder can stream.
- **The Linux tarball runs on other distros.** 0.8.3's tarball did not start on Arch because it linked the build machine's FFmpeg libraries; it now encodes through the system `ffmpeg` program and links none, and was unpacked in Arch and Fedora containers before release.

**Linux desktops**
- **GNOME with no one at the desk (optional, off by default):** Settings → Connection → "Unattended on GNOME" starts a screen and input session with no dialog, through GNOME's own services, with GNOME's screen-sharing indicator showing (limit 75). GNOME's ordinary portal needs someone to click through a dialog, and its "Allow Remote Interaction" switch starts off, which leaves a session view-only.
- **The firewall row reads nftables and iptables** (before, only ufw and firewalld), and the Pair page and Settings → Other computers say on Linux when the firewall shuts the control or stream port, with the exact command to open it. Arch's stock rules, which let in ssh only, are named.

**Security and fixes**
- Every packet Pocketdesk parses now has a size limit, and six fuzzers run in CI (30 seconds each on pull requests, 5 minutes each nightly). An oversized clipboard from another computer is dropped on the link, and both ends are told instead of nothing happening.
- **On Windows, state files save while another program holds them** (an antivirus scan, a backup or sync client, an editor). Before, a pairing, an unpair or a remote revoke could fail with "Access is denied" and a revoked device stayed trusted; saving now retries for about half a second, and a crash's leftover temporary copies are swept when the server starts.
- A phone's location answer, a fix or a refusal, now reaches the computer, and a fix that never comes no longer leaves the phone answering no later ask (both found in the 2026-11-01 device batch).
- A turned-down session no longer stamps the computer's card "Used just now", a computer's approval asks by the computer's name, and a demotion notice names the computer that introduced you even after it was removed.
- A security review of each feature above found and fixed more: for example a kept-folders run's deletions held to the safe side on the phone and again on the computer, links refused on the way to a kept file, a hotspot stop that fails kept and tried again, and a watch pairing that cannot be opened by the six digits alone.
- SECURITY.md has seventeen new known limits (73 to 89): approving `sudo` with your phone (73), the phone as a camera (74), unattended GNOME (75), the phone's location (76), the direct link (77), the phone's apps (78), hands-free apps (79), kept folders (80), pins and shared drops (81), the wake helper (82), apps in windows and keys to taps through Shizuku (83), watch controls (84), the phone's hotspot (85), lending a window (86, Windows 88, GNOME 89) and dragging one across (87). Read them before turning these on for a computer or phone someone else can reach.

## Upgrade notes

- **Lending windows, dragging them across and smooth keyframes are on when you update** unless your config.toml already says otherwise: a setting you saved as off stays off. Lending and dragging only ever reach your own computers paired both ways with the Input permission.
- **Update every device** that should use the new computer-to-computer parts; an older end refuses or ignores what it does not know, and nothing breaks.
- **Owner features need your own phone's pairing.** Kept folders, the wake helper and introductions work only for a phone paired with the computer's own code (the Pair page, not "Someone else's"); a phone paired as someone else's or with a guest grant is refused.
- **New Android permissions are asked only when you turn the feature on:** location ("Give my computer my location") and nearby devices (Bluetooth, "Watch controls"). Shizuku's own dialog appears once when you turn on a Shizuku feature, and the phone never tells you to install Shizuku or turn on wireless debugging.
- **The Linux tarball now needs the `ffmpeg` program** (install.sh offers to install it when missing) and glibc 2.39 or newer. Because it no longer links FFmpeg, it asks for a keyframe on its two-second schedule rather than at once, and cannot change the bitrate in place. The .deb and the AUR package keep the in-process encoder.
- **Stock Fedora** has no libx264 and no H.264 encoding in its own Mesa: install `openh264` for software encoding, or RPM Fusion's `ffmpeg` or its freeworld VA drivers for hardware.
- **Folders kept on the computer** are on by default on the computer's side but do nothing until an owner phone picks a folder; files land under Documents/Pocketdesk phones/ (or the folder you choose), up to a 50 GB cap. Turn it off in Settings if you do not want it. **The direct link** is also on by default but starts only when you ask for it on the Pair page.

## Known issues

- On KDE through a desktop portal, an app that scrolls only by high-resolution wheel steps still won't scroll: the portal sends pixels with none. A touchpad's fine scrolling works elsewhere in this release.
- A phone app's window is sized when it opens: resizing the window on the computer scales the picture only. A keymap is fixed to the picture's shape, so a window made at another shape needs its keys moved. Keys to taps has no gamepad mapping and its aim lifts after 150 ms of stillness.
- Turning off Windows' own hotspot settings during a direct link is not noticed until the link's idle time ends it.
- When GNOME's "Allow Remote Interaction" is off, the computer tells the phone the session is view-only but the phone app shows no banner for it yet.
- Android 10 to 13 are untested for windows of their own, and a foreground-service start from the background may be refused by Android on some phones (the page then opens the app on the phone's screen).

## Not yet checked on a device

These work in tests, and some ran on real hardware from a script or between throwaway servers (the OPPO against servers on a Linux laptop, in the 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-01 batches, which ticked remote revoke, introductions, the card menu, the front camera at 1080p, the phone's own location decisions, and the phone-apps list and opens), but not yet:
- **Phone apps and hands-free apps** (checklist §258, §259, §261): a secure lock, a second computer's ask, Android 15 or 16, the desktop's page and window by hand, whether ColorOS shows the screen-sharing button to the control service, a paused share and its resume, Extend Unlock, and the Start menu and applications menu pins.
- **Apps in windows of their own, keys to taps and the phone's hotspot** (§263, §265, §266): none has run on any phone. The first check is whether Android's tethering manager call starts a hotspot on Android 11 to 15 and on the OPPO, and whether the helper's display, launch and injection work with Shizuku.
- **Phone folders kept** (§260) and **a spare phone as the wake helper** (§262): the OPPO as the helper on a home Wi-Fi with a second phone away and a real sleeping computer, and the kept folders' run, deletions, cap and schedule on a phone.
- **The Wear OS tile** (§264): nothing has run on a real watch. The first check is whether a Wear OS watch can connect to the phone's Bluetooth service.
- **The phone's camera and location** (§252, §255): a real video call, OBS and GNOME Snapshot, Stop from the phone's notification, and a real session on a desk; location with the screen off and "Allow all the time", with Exact, and with two computers.
- **The direct link** (§256, §257): the hotspot itself on a throwaway adapter, the second-interface road, the OPPO scanning and joining, the idle timer and the restore of the owner's Windows hotspot settings.
- **Approve with my phone** (§250): a real fingerprint on `sudo`, polkit and the lock screen, and pinning with Key Attestation (the OPPO has no screen lock).
- **GNOME at a real desk** (§254, §100): unattended with and without a second monitor, an older GNOME, and "Allow Remote Interaction" off.
- **Fit the screen to this window** (§253), **fine scrolling** (§249: KDE and GNOME portals, uinput, a Windows host, the phone's trackpad, shared input between two computers), **shared input** driving for real (§247, §251) and **software encoding on a real stock Fedora machine** (§248).
- **The Linux firewall row in the desktop app** (§246): the Pair page's line going away within 30 seconds of the ports being opened, the `nft insert` lines run by hand, and an iptables DROP policy.
- **0.8.3's own open items** (§240, §242, §243, §245): Keys by position with real layouts and games, the version line across a release gap, sound and TalkBack on the card menu, and the phone's second screen on Hyprland; and from §241 two computers paired both ways and a one-way computer's card.
- **Windows across computers** (§267 to §282): lending and borrowing ran on headless Sway and GNOME sessions on a Linux laptop. Still owed: Hyprland live, a Windows computer lending for real (never run on Windows yet), KDE (lends nothing yet), dragging past the edge between two real desks, and smooth keyframes viewed on a phone.
- **Updating** from 0.8.3 to this release on a phone, and a clean install.

The full list is in [the checklist](https://github.com/sreevarshan-xenoz/Pocketdesk/blob/main/docs/device-verification-checklist.md) (§246 on are 0.9.0's) and, by where each can run, in [docs/owed-checks.md](https://github.com/sreevarshan-xenoz/Pocketdesk/blob/main/docs/owed-checks.md).
